title: nOS — cortex-lang (execution)
description: What the cortex executor ran, from the events it emits. Companion to 25-loop (the self-improvement ledger) and to files/anatomy/cortex/scripts/corpus-gen.ts (the grammar's shape).

options.content:
**cortex-lang, as the executor actually runs it.** Every panel reads the `cortex_stage_*` events the executor emits — `task` is the opcode, `actor_action_id` is the chain (`cx-…`), and `result_json` carries the stage index, its effect and its row count.

This is the RUNTIME half. Whether a chain is *well-formed* is decided before it gets here, by `analyzeCortex` — and that check constrains stages, never their order (`files/anatomy/cortex/scripts/corpus-gen.ts` measures it: 20 306 of 20 306 composed chains validate). So nothing on this page should be read as evidence that a chain was a good idea.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT actor_action_id) AS chains FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_begin'
targets.queryText: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT actor_action_id) AS chains FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_begin'

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS stages FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_finish'
targets.queryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS stages FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_finish'

panels.title: Stages that began and never finished
panels.description: A begin with no matching finish is a stage the executor entered and never left. Zero is the good state; it is computed by set difference rather than by comparing two counts, because equal counts can hide a lost pair.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS unfinished FROM (
  SELECT actor_action_id, task, json_extract(result_json,'$.index') AS ix
    FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_begin'
  EXCEPT
  SELECT actor_action_id, task, json_extract(result_json,'$.index')
    FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_finish')
targets.queryText:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS unfinished FROM (
  SELECT actor_action_id, task, json_extract(result_json,'$.index') AS ix
    FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_begin'
  EXCEPT
  SELECT actor_action_id, task, json_extract(result_json,'$.index')
    FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_finish')

panels.title: Dispatch rejects
panels.description: A chain the executor refused to dispatch. The gate that refused it is in the table below.

targets.rawQueryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rejects FROM events WHERE type='cortex_dispatch_reject'
targets.queryText: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rejects FROM events WHERE type='cortex_dispatch_reject'

panels.title: Chains by length — the panel this page was built to show
panels.description: MEASURED 2026-08-29: 390 chains, every one of them a SINGLE STAGE. cortex-lang is a pipeline IR and no pipeline has ever run through it. That is not a fault in the executor — it is what the callers ask for — but it means the composition half of the language is unexercised, and a row here with stages_in_chain > 1 is the first evidence otherwise.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT stages AS stages_in_chain, COUNT(*) AS chains FROM (
  SELECT actor_action_id, COUNT(*) AS stages
    FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_begin' GROUP BY actor_action_id
) GROUP BY stages ORDER BY stages
targets.queryText:
SELECT stages AS stages_in_chain, COUNT(*) AS chains FROM (
  SELECT actor_action_id, COUNT(*) AS stages
    FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_begin' GROUP BY actor_action_id
) GROUP BY stages ORDER BY stages

panels.title: Opcodes — what the estate actually calls
panels.description: Read beside the registry: an opcode the registry declares and this table never shows is a capability nothing has ever exercised.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT task AS opcode, COUNT(*) AS stages,
       SUM(json_extract(result_json,'$.effect')='read') AS read_effect,
       SUM(json_extract(result_json,'$.code') IS NOT NULL) AS returned_a_code,
       SUM(COALESCE(json_extract(result_json,'$.rows'),0)) AS rows_returned
  FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_finish'
 GROUP BY task ORDER BY stages DESC
targets.queryText:
SELECT task AS opcode, COUNT(*) AS stages,
       SUM(json_extract(result_json,'$.effect')='read') AS read_effect,
       SUM(json_extract(result_json,'$.code') IS NOT NULL) AS returned_a_code,
       SUM(COALESCE(json_extract(result_json,'$.rows'),0)) AS rows_returned
  FROM events WHERE type='cortex_stage_finish'
 GROUP BY task ORDER BY stages DESC

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT b.actor_action_id AS chain, MIN(b.ts) AS started, COUNT(*) AS stages,
       group_concat(b.task, ' | ') AS pipeline,
       CAST((julianday(MAX(f.ts)) - julianday(MIN(b.ts))) * 86400000 AS INT) AS ms
  FROM events b
  LEFT JOIN events f ON f.actor_action_id = b.actor_action_id
                    AND f.type = 'cortex_stage_finish'
 WHERE b.type = 'cortex_stage_begin'
 GROUP BY b.actor_action_id ORDER BY started DESC LIMIT 40
targets.queryText:
SELECT b.actor_action_id AS chain, MIN(b.ts) AS started, COUNT(*) AS stages,
       group_concat(b.task, ' | ') AS pipeline,
       CAST((julianday(MAX(f.ts)) - julianday(MIN(b.ts))) * 86400000 AS INT) AS ms
  FROM events b
  LEFT JOIN events f ON f.actor_action_id = b.actor_action_id
                    AND f.type = 'cortex_stage_finish'
 WHERE b.type = 'cortex_stage_begin'
 GROUP BY b.actor_action_id ORDER BY started DESC LIMIT 40

panels.title: Refusals, by the gate that refused
panels.description: Empty means no chain was ever refused, which is not the same as none being refusable.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT json_extract(result_json,'$.gate') AS gate, task AS opcode,
       COUNT(*) AS refusals, MAX(ts) AS last_seen
  FROM events WHERE type='cortex_dispatch_reject'
 GROUP BY gate, opcode ORDER BY refusals DESC
targets.queryText:
SELECT json_extract(result_json,'$.gate') AS gate, task AS opcode,
       COUNT(*) AS refusals, MAX(ts) AS last_seen
  FROM events WHERE type='cortex_dispatch_reject'
 GROUP BY gate, opcode ORDER BY refusals DESC
